The Past Perfect and Past Perfect Continuous Tenses
You use both the Past Perfect and Past Perfect Continuous tenses to talk about past actions that happened before another past action. What are the differences between them?
Refer to the chart for a summary of the differences between the Past Perfect and Past Perfect Continuous tenses.

Perfect Infinitives and Perfect Continuous Infinitive - Review
You use Perfect Infinitives in the same way as you use other Perfect tenses (to talk about the past). You can use them to talk about unreal situations in the past.

The Perfect Infinitive refers to a time before the preceding verb.
You use the Perfect Infinitive in the result clause of the third conditional.
You use the modals could have, might have, ought to have, should have, would have and needn't have + the past participle to talk about the unreal past.
If the teacher had known about the strike, she would probably have avoided going to work.
The Perfect Continuous Infinitive refers to a time before that of the preceding verb and expresses an action in progress or happening over a period of time.
You use the Perfect Infinitive Continuous after modal verbs and after appear and seem, but it can also be used after happen, pretend and the passive of believe, know, report, say, understand.

Write a tall tale you heard from a distant relative.
Instructions: Complete the following steps. Fill in the Self-Assessment.

images.text:
Bernard had continued to tell Jerry fascinating exploits about his life. He described how he'd been traveling through Europe, earning money as a model. He admitted to have been having an affair with the French prime minister's niece – and how he would have liked to have married her.
He told Jerry how he'd begun working as a journalist in London and had grown to be one of the most popular war correspondents in Britain. Jerry gained respect for Bernard. He wondered what it was like to have become a famous journalist! Bernard had also told Jerry about the books he had written. To his amazement, they had even made a movie out of one.

One evening, Jerry had been sitting waiting for the genial Bernard to come to dinner. If you were to have asked anyone they would have said that he was never late. Jerry had begun to worry for the senior. He'd called Bernard's home, but no one appeared to have been answering.
Jerry had Bernard's address, but he had never been to his place. When Jerry drove up to the house, he was more than a little surprised. It was a small, dark street wedged into a poor area. The house itself looked to have seen better days.
"What about all the money he made from being a journalist?" Jerry wondered. "Bernard seemed to have been stretching the truth!"

"Bernard?" he called out.
"Over here ..." a faint voice cried out.
Jerry followed the voice to the back door. Bernard had been lying there next to a stepladder. He appeared to have been trying to fix a light.
"Thank goodness you came!" Bernard said. Jerry believed him to have been grateful, but also thought him to be extremely embarrassed. Bernard seemed to have been telling rather tall tales!
Jerry had taken Bernard to the hospital and assured him that he was not angry. That he had been enjoying the stories too much to complain. The stories had been exciting! Maybe, he ventured, they could write a book together ...
